current.text: He is back from the torn ACL that cost him all of last season. He is expected to be ready to start on opening night.
At media day he made troubling comments about his knee and said he does not feel like himself.
He is the projected starting point guard. Amen Thompson moves off point guard. If VanVleet has a setback, Marcus Smart would start in his place.

Experts expect the Rockets to limit his minutes early and rest him on some back-to-backs. Lloyd projects about 32 minutes: near 30 at the start, rising to about 34. Another expert says he could reach 35 minutes by the end of the year.
Josh expects missed games and stretches of bad shooting as he comes back from the ACL injury.
Houston has a crowded guard rotation and many other ball handlers, so Lloyd is not counting on high assists from him.
Experts put his category league value around picks 107 to 135, about round 10, as a late point guard flyer. His ESPN rank of 74 is too high. Do not take him anywhere near pick 42.
With our March 28 end date, the Rockets play 3, 3 and 4 games in the fantasy playoff weeks, 10 games in total. That is a weak playoff schedule.
The Rockets have only 14 back-to-backs this season.
Houston is projected to win 54 games. The team is expected to play it safe in the regular season and not chase seeding.

durable.text: He tore his ACL and missed the full 2025-26 season.
He is a very poor shooter from the field, worst on twos. His FG% is a clear weakness on real volume.
He is a good three-point shooter and gives good assists and steals, with fairly low scoring.
He takes very good care of the ball and keeps his turnovers low.
He has historically been worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: Yahoo values him at 1 USD (rank 129) and ESPN at 5 USD (rank 74), and he went for 1 USD in our league last season. Experts rank him around 107 to 135, so in our 144-player draft he is a 1 to 3 USD late guard, mainly for punt FG% builds that want threes, assists and steals plus a decent FT% (84.7%). Early in the season, check whether his minutes climb from about 30 toward 34, how often he sits back-to-backs, and whether his assists hold up next to the other Houston ball handlers. Remember the weak 10-game playoff schedule.
